claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my one child - their name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm happy to help you with your Child Benefit query for Alex.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 16, their education or training status is important for determining eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, GCSEs, or equivalent), or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex actually left school recently, but they've just registered with the local careers service to figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify a few things:

1. How long ago did Alex leave school?
2. When Alex registered with the local careers service, was this to be considered for a place on an approved training course or employment? In other words, has Alex registered for education, training, or work through an official careers service or similar body (sometimes called "approved body")?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was pretty recent - they left school just a few weeks ago. And yes, they registered with the careers service to get help finding training or work options. It's one of those official programmes where they help young people figure out their next steps after leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is really helpful information.

Just a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

1. Is Alex currently living with you?
2. Are you responsible for Alex financially (i.e., do you pay for their food, clothing, accommodation, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me, and yes, I'm responsible for them financially - I pay for everything they need like food, clothes, and all their living expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more question: Are you currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex has recently left school (within the past few weeks)
- Alex has registered with an official careers service to be considered for training or work
- Alex lives with you and you are financially responsible for them
- You live in England

Let me confirm your eligibility now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex:**
- ✅ Alex is 16 years old, which is within the eligible age range
- ✅ Although Alex has left school, they have registered with an official careers service to explore training or employment options. This qualifies as being registered with an "approved body," which extends Child Benefit eligibility
- ✅ Alex lives with you in the UK
- ✅ You are financially responsible for Alex

**Important note:** This eligibility will continue as long as Alex remains registered with the careers service or starts approved training/education. If Alex's situation changes (for example, they start working more than 24 hours a week, or they are no longer registered with the careers service), you would need to inform the Child Benefit Office as this could affect your eligibility.

If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
